R060-01.notes: Final paragraph states the lesson: drivers respond to prices and benefits are easier to see once lived with. B (London vs Stockholm comparison) not made; C is explicitly denied ('not that a price solves every transportation problem'); D is only one detail (Stockholm pre-trial opposition).

R060-02.notes: Opposition before trial, majority approval after seven months illustrates 'benefits easier to see once people have lived with it.' A contradicts the text (most opposed beforehand); B unsupported; D confuses cause (the vote did not cause the traffic drop).

R060-03.notes: Direct detail: combined trips, skipped optional ones, switched to buses and trains. A is the gridlock-at-edges prediction the passage refutes; B and C unsupported. Factually consistent with Stockholm trial evaluations.

R060-04.notes: Sentence before the example: same fee is not the same burden. C (exemption) goes beyond the passage; D contradicts 'no one seriously disputes that a congestion charge can cut traffic'; A irrelevant.

R060-05.notes: 'Their fairness depends on what a city does with the money and on what alternatives it offers.' A contradicts 'does not mean that charges are a mistake'; B is the supporters' view B rejects; C contradicts B's skepticism about referenda.

R060-06.notes: Context glosses 'neutral' as everyone pays the same fee and everyone benefits, so 'treating everyone the same way.' C is the common-meaning trap; the 'in a debate' qualifier rules it out. B and D do not fit context.

R060-07.notes: B's last paragraph: early public support is not proof that a charge treats everyone well; majority benefit can come with minority burden. C overstates (B never calls a vote invalid); D contradicts B's first sentence; A is the opposite.

R060-08.notes: A documents changed travel behavior; B concedes charges cut traffic, which entails changed travel. B is the closest rival: Passage B stresses revenue use, but it never ranks revenue above traffic reduction and A does not address revenue. A and D are rejected by Passage B.

R060-09.notes: The example contrasts revenue that improves bus service with revenue that 'disappears into a general budget.' C contradicts 'identical'; A and D are not mentioned in the sentence.

R060-10.notes: B centers on the distribution of burden (lawyer vs aide, minority bearing the cost). B, C and D are all Passage A's focus or are conceded by Passage B.
